findings.title: `sed -i ''` only works with macOS/BSD sed and breaks on Linux.
findings.body: GNU sed (Linux) reads the `''` after `-i` as the sed script, then treats the real expression as a filename. When `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` already exists in the env file, the update fails, yet the script still prints "Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL". Use a form both seds accept, e.g. `sed -i.bak ... && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`.

findings.title: Unrelated change to how the dev cron script runs.
findings.body: Swapping `ts-node` for `npx tsx` in `dev:cron` changes the tooling every developer uses to run the cron tester. The cache status and actions feature doesn't need it. `npx` may also download `tsx` from the network when it isn't installed locally. Move this to its own PR.

findings.title: Calling updateMany with an empty data object probably won't bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes no fields. Prisma may treat an update with empty `data` as a no-op, and it does not reliably set the `@updatedAt` column when no field changes. If so, the comment's goal of refreshing `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is never met, and every cache refresh still makes an extra database round trip. Also, the new UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so nothing in this PR uses this write. If the timestamp is needed, set it explicitly with `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`. If it isn't, remove the call.

findings.title: Existing cache rows get the migration time as `updatedAt`, so old caches look freshly updated.
findings.body: Every `CalendarCache` row that exists when this runs gets `updatedAt = NOW()`. The new `connectedCalendars` handler and `CredentialActionsDropdown` show `cacheUpdatedAt` as the cache status. Right after deploy, every credential will show its cache as just updated, even if the data is stale or expired, until the cache is rewritten. Fix: backfill from a better value. For example, add the column, run `UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - interval '...'` (or similar), then set the default. Another option is to make the column nullable and show 'unknown' for old rows.

findings.title: Delete cache fails for credentials the user doesn't own directly (delegation or team credentials), even though the UI offers it.
findings.body: The dropdown shows "Delete cached data" whenever a Google credential has a cache, including delegation credentials, where `canDisconnect` is false. The handler only accepts a `Credential` row whose `userId` equals the current user, so a delegation credential (an in-memory or synthetic id, not owned by the user) or a team credential is always rejected. In that case the user just sees "Error deleting cache". The handler also throws a plain `Error`, which reaches the client as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN. Fix one of two ways: resolve ownership the same way `connectedCalendars` does (only allow ids returned for the user), or hide the action for delegation credentials. In either case throw a `TRPCError` with the right code.

findings.title: Unrelated webhook tunnel script that writes to a .env path relative to the working directory.
findings.body: Cache status and cache deletion don't need a Tunnelmole helper, so this script is outside the request. It also writes `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` to `../.env` relative to wherever it is run from, so running it from another directory creates or edits an unexpected `.env` file. Move it to a separate PR, or at least resolve the path relative to the script's own location.

findings.title: The cache timestamp is always formatted with the "en-US" locale.
findings.body: The surrounding text is translated through `t()`, but the date uses a fixed `"en-US"` locale. Users in other locales will see US date order, for example 7/15/25 instead of 15/7/25. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) instead.

findings.title: The generated warning comment no longer matches the SQL below it.
findings.body: The comment says the required column is added "without a default value" and that this fails on a non-empty table. Line 9 now adds a default, so the warning is wrong and could mislead people about whether the migration is safe. Remove the stale warning block.

findings.title: Access-denied error is a plain Error, so the client gets a 500 instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN.
findings.body: A user who calls this with a credential they do not own, or with a team or delegation credential, gets a plain `Error`. tRPC turns that into INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so the caller cannot tell the request was refused from a server failure, and the error is logged as a server failure. Throw a `TRPCError` with code `NOT_FOUND` (or `FORBIDDEN`) instead. This needs an import of `TRPCError` from `@trpc/server`.

findings.title: Added SelectedCalendar fields (updatedAt, googleChannelId) that nothing in the PR uses.
findings.body: The type here and the user select in `user.ts` now include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but the cache status shown in the UI comes from `CalendarCache`, not from these fields. They look like leftovers from an earlier approach and add data to a shared user query. Remove them unless something needs them.

held.title: The DB default `NOW()` may not match the Prisma schema, which would cause migration drift.
held.body: This migration was edited by hand to add `DEFAULT NOW()`, and the warning comment above it still describes the generated version with no default. If `schema.prisma` declares the field as `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` without `@default(now())`, Prisma expects the column to have no DB default. The next `prisma migrate dev` will then report drift and generate a migration that drops the default. I couldn't see the schema.prisma change from here. Fix: make the schema field `@default(now()) @updatedAt` so the schema matches this SQL, and remove the stale warning comment.
